name: Elegance and Insight Rubric v3
description: Six sub-criteria rated H/M/L; count H scores to get final score. Hard caps for missing conceptual core or explanatory force. Worked examples at all five score levels.

criteria.name: SC-A: Conceptual Core
criteria.description: Names the structural reason why the result holds.
checks: Does it identify a key structural fact, invariant, symmetry, or contradiction?
Or does it apply an algorithm without naming the underlying mechanism?

criteria.name: SC-B: Economy of Means
checks: Could the insight be stated in 1-3 sentences?
Or is there a long chain of manipulations where a shorter path exists?

criteria.name: SC-C: Explanatory Force
checks: After reading, can a student apply the principle to a new problem?
Or is it purely procedural with only local step-by-step justifications?

criteria.name: SC-D: Avoidance of Mechanical Grinding
checks: Does it take the principled path over computer assistance or case enumeration?
Does it note why the elegant approach is preferred?

criteria.name: SC-E: Generativity
criteria.description: The insight extends beyond this specific problem.
checks: Is the approach or principle clearly generalizable?
Does the answer name the general pattern?

criteria.name: SC-F: Non-Obviousness
criteria.description: Reveals something a skilled student would NOT immediately know.
checks: Is the key move surprising or non-trivial?
Does it bypass an expected route in a clever way?

aggregation: Count H scores: 5-6H=1.0, 4H=0.75, 3H=0.5, 2H=0.25, 0-1H=0.0. SC-A=L caps at 0.25; SC-C=L caps at 0.5.

scores.1.0: 5-6 sub-criteria HIGH: avoids computation, names general principle, surprises
scores.0.75: 4 sub-criteria HIGH: elegant and explanatory but does not explicitly generalize or surprise
scores.0.5: 3 sub-criteria HIGH: identifies right approach but resolution is algorithmic
scores.0.25: 2 sub-criteria HIGH: well-organized but mechanical; HOW not WHY
scores.0.0: 0-1 HIGH: bare result, link, or wall of computation
